title: Stress — very long work experience (~8-10k chars)

data.marketLevelRationale: Candidate demonstrates 5+ roles with exposure to modern infrastructure tooling (Kubernetes, Terraform, Kafka) and polyglot capabilities (React, Node, Go, Python), indicating beyond junior-level technical breadth. However, without evidence of architectural ownership, system design decisions at scale, or cross-functional leadership, the profile does not support senior classification. Mid-level professionals typically have 4-7 years of experience with full-stack project delivery and emerging systems thinking—this profile aligns with that band.

salaryRange.note: Ho Chi Minh City market rates for mid-level full-stack/platform engineers are 25–35% lower than Western equivalents. Candidate's target of 4000–6000 USD/month is above realistic market clearing for this level in Vietnam; achievable only at top-tier fintechs or foreign multinational subsidiaries. Local market supports 2800–4200 USD/month for proven mid-level talent with platform engineering exposure.

coreStrengths.evidence: Kubernetes, Terraform, Kafka, AWS, and Postgres demonstrate hands-on experience with production platform patterns; indicates practical systems thinking beyond CRUD application development.

React, Node, Go, and Python across multiple roles suggests adaptability and reduced onboarding friction when context shifts; Go and Python in particular signal willingness to work outside web-first domains.
5+ distinct roles with project-level bullets indicate sustained ability to scope, execute, and ship; reduces execution risk in hiring.

criticalGaps.gap: No evidence of platform or infrastructure architecture leadership
criticalGaps.impact: Stated interest in platform engineering but profile lacks proof of designing systems, defining standards, or mentoring others on infrastructure decisions. Platform engineering roles at mid-to-senior level expect thought leadership and visibility into tooling strategy. Without this, candidate appears to be a skilled platform engineer user, not a platform engineer builder.

criticalGaps.gap: Unclear depth in distributed systems or high-scale operational concerns
criticalGaps.impact: Exposure to Kafka and Kubernetes is noted, but no detail on debugging distributed failures, capacity planning, observability strategy, or running systems under production load. Platform engineering requires deep operational maturity; if experience is limited to happy-path configuration, candidate will struggle with incident response and resilience design.

criticalGaps.gap: Limited evidence of cross-functional collaboration or influence
criticalGaps.impact: Platform engineering is inherently a multiplier role requiring buy-in from dozens of teams. Without examples of working across silos, driving adoption, or communicating trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders, candidate may underperform in consensus-building and organizational influence.

criticalGaps.gap: No signal on thought leadership or continuous learning cadence
criticalGaps.impact: Platform engineering moves rapidly. Absence of conference talks, blog posts, open-source contributions, or certifications suggests passive rather than active engagement with field evolution. This may indicate slower adaptation to emerging tooling.

data.uniqueValueProposition: Full-stack operator with modern infrastructure fluency who can own platform reliability and developer experience simultaneously—rare combination in Vietnam market, but unproven as a systems architect.
data.readinessNote: Candidate has the technical toolkit and breadth for a mid-level platform engineering role (score ~60–70), but lacks proof of system design authority or operational depth at scale (penalties of -20 to -30). Score reflects technical capability offset by demonstrated gaps in the core responsibilities of platform engineering. Immediate readiness for mid-level IC platform role is moderate; readiness for stretch senior role is low. Salary expectation (4000–6000 USD) exceeds realistic Ho Chi Minh City market by 30–50%; this misalignment and potential resulting role mismatch further reduces readiness for stated target. With 12–18 months of focused platform leadership experience and a downward salary adjustment, readiness could climb to 75–80.
